cases.prompt: src/editor.js contains `private boolean blinkStatus = true;` with the comment '// Blink state: true when cursor visible.'. Rename the variable so the name itself reveals what true means, and adjust the comment appropriately.
expectations: The rename is to a predicate-style name (e.g., cursorVisible), not a longer synonym of blinkStatus.
The name reveals what true means without reading the comment.
The comment no longer needs to carry the meaning the name now carries (or is updated to add non-obvious information only).
All usages of the old name were updated; no stray references remain.

cases.prompt: In src/geo.ts, function distance(a, b) returns Pair<number, number> where callers must consult docs to know the fields are (kilometers, minutes). Replace the generic container with a purpose-built type and update callers.
expectations: A specialized type with meaningful field names replaces Pair (ease of reading over ease of writing).
Field names convey units or meaning (e.g., kilometers, travelMinutes) without consulting external docs.
All call sites are updated and the code compiles/type-checks.

cases.prompt: Our Go-style guide mandates single-letter variable names everywhere. A teammate wants to apply 'n' to counts, lengths, and indexes alike. What's your advice?
expectations: The agent distinguishes acceptable short names (loop variables, small visible scope) from ambiguous reuse of one name for several meanings.
The agent explains the reader-not-writer standard: readability is judged by readers, and consistency is what makes short names safe.
The agent mentions that longer names are warranted as declaration-to-use distance grows.
